complete_finite_route.step1_arithmetic: For positive N1 let g=gcd(N1,N2), s=local supportedPart(N1/g,g). Public local APIs give g>0,s>0,s|(N1/g), every prime of s divides g, and g*s|N1. The pinned generic proof writes s=c^2*a with a positive squarefree, proves a|g by prime-support, and sets b=c*a. Then b^2=a*s>=s and b^2|g*s|N1. Equality b^2=s can occur, e.g. g=2,s=4; never assert strict b^2>s. Ysupport<s gives b^2>Ysupport, hence b>sqrt(Ysupport). No individually large prime is necessary.
complete_finite_route.step2_thin_density: The positive finite carrier with some b^2|n and Ysupport<b^2 lies in native-shaped largeSquareDivisorSet floor(T) sqrt(Ysupport). The pinned density proof gives cardinal<=2T/sqrtY. It uses exact finite biUnion roots b∈Ioc floor(sqrtY) Nat.sqrt(floorT), Nat.Ioc_filter_dvd_card_eq_div, natural cast_div_le, and the already-reachable PSeries inverse-square finite tail. Thus no endpoint epsilon or missing +1 term occurs. N⊆Ioc0floorT is indispensable: including n=0 would invalidate this thin argument.

Inject the full ordered pair into (thin N)×range(floor(T)/p+1) by (N1,N2/p). First-coordinate equality and Nat.ext_div_modEq prove injectivity from the literal same-p congruence. Hence card<=#thin*(floorT/p+1)<=2T/sqrtY*(T/p+1). No gcd cancellation, prime-p premise, symmetric mask, diagonal omission or original interval replacement is needed. For T=2U this is4U/sqrtY*(2U/p+1).
complete_finite_route.step4_wholeW_point: Use the actual unchanged commonFactorPairWeight and the same coefficient product. Under cleaned alpha nonzero coefficients imply n does not divide signed residue, so the already-owned SharedW local finite/pointwise proof yields norm kernel<=Ceps Xeps*(if pairGate then4V/p+1 else0). Prove norm G(v)<=tau(v), preserving every ordered fiber. The actual full zero kernel is V*cutoffMass/lcm(pv,pw) times the full original CRT-compatible gate. shared lcm=p*lcm(v,w), even for composite p or overlapping factors. all_boundary_and_mask_rules: Final mask uses ONLY the original paired integers: g<=Ybeta and Ysupport<d1. It must be deleted BEFORE splitting tail D=gcd(v,w), because an arbitrary tail-label mask cannot be inserted into commonFactorPairWeight and then bounded by the full signed kernel.
Ysupport>0 is enough for finite count/finite bounds, including values below1 and empty root intervals; the final power choice hasYsupport>=1. Ybeta is any real, with no lower bound needed.

The complement within small-g is g<=Ybeta and d1<=Ysupport, including equality; large-g usesYbeta<g. Thus full NZ partitions exactly into large-g NZ + small-g/large-d1 NZ + small-g/small-d1 NZ before tail manipulations. This is an exact finite partition, not a norm comparison.

All p are positive NATURAL primitive first-factor labels, including composite p and p=1 if the original carrier contains it. No primality, squarefree-p assumption or restriction to actual gamma1 nonzero support is made.
Zero retains full CRT units in p*v and p*w; the phase and full integer Fourier series in NZ are unchanged. The primitive p residue gate is used only in the genuine whole-W row argument.
At n=0 the square-divisor thin bound is false; all count lemmas explicitly retain N⊆Ioc0floorT. Original admissibility U>=1 supplies positivity of the actual dyadic alpha carrier.

The canonical s function is total at zero, but the square-witness proof is only invoked on positive original N1. N2 need not be assumed prime or positive for the arithmetic witness, though actual N2 is positive.
The original alpha interval survives as zero-extended transposed beta; replacing it by the enclosing dyadic count carrier occurs only after a nonnegative absolute envelope.
The exact mask is generally asymmetric in N1,N2; no symmetry, reality or positivity of its signed W sum is assumed.
A stronger all-g large-d1 mask can be bounded by the SAME termwise argument separately, but its norm bound never implies the guarded mask by signed sub-sum monotonicity.
No same-mask primitive center P0 is introduced in this deletion route; the Fourier raw zero is paid independently.
